1	//// Hermetic-test seam for the agent-dev pipeline.
2	////
3	//// Each scenario registers one typed handler per activity through
4	//// `aion/testing.mock_activity` — the same names, codecs, and dispatch path
5	//// the deployed workflow uses, with the test's handlers standing where the
6	//// agent-dev worker stands in production. `passing/0` is the all-green
7	//// baseline; scenarios override individual handlers with a record update.
8	////
9	//// The default dev handler ECHOES its prompt into the dev report, so a
10	//// review handler can observe (statelessly) whether its feedback made the
11	//// round trip through the dev session — the seam the review-fail scenario
12	//// keys on. `counter_next` (test FFI, process-dictionary scoped) is the
13	//// seam for handlers that must vary by call number, like a gate that fails
14	//// once then passes.
15	
16	import agent_dev/activities
17	import agent_dev_io as io
18	import aion/agent.{type AgentOutcome, AgentOutcome}
19	import aion/error
20	import aion/testing
21	
22	/// One handler per activity the pipeline dispatches.
23	///
24	/// The three agent handlers stay TEXT handlers: a scenario scripts what the
25	/// agent said, and `register` wraps each in the same text-to-record mapping
26	/// the production worker's harness boundary performs (the canonical
27	/// agent-outcome record, `stop_reason: "end_turn"` on a completed round).
28	pub type Handlers {
29	  Handlers(
30	    provision: fn(io.ProvisionInput) ->
31	      Result(io.Workspace, error.ActivityError),
32	    scout: fn(String) -> Result(String, error.ActivityError),
33	    dev: fn(String) -> Result(String, error.ActivityError),
34	    review: fn(String) -> Result(String, error.ActivityError),
35	    gate: fn(io.Workspace) -> Result(io.GateDetail, error.ActivityError),
36	    land: fn(io.LandInput) -> Result(io.LandOutput, error.ActivityError),
37	  )
38	}
39	
40	/// Per-process invocation counter (1 on the first call for a key). The
41	/// harness runs handlers in the test's own process, so this is test-scoped.
42	@external(erlang, "agent_dev_test_ffi", "counter_next")
43	pub fn counter_next(key: String) -> Int
44	
45	/// A reviewer's passing terminal text: prose first, the JSON verdict at the
46	/// end — exactly what the in-prompt contract asks for.
47	pub const pass_verdict_text = "The work is complete and production-ready. No blockers found.\n{\"pass\": true, \"blockers\": [], \"summary\": \"all acceptance criteria met\"}"
48	
49	/// A reviewer's failing terminal text carrying one blocker.
50	pub fn fail_verdict_text(blocker: String) -> String {
51	  "Blockers were found.\n{\"pass\": false, \"blockers\": [\""
52	  <> blocker
53	  <> "\"], \"summary\": \"changes required\"}"
54	}
55	
56	/// The workflow input every scenario starts from. Both caps are required
57	/// fields, so each test states them explicitly.
58	pub fn base_input() -> io.Input {
59	  io.Input(
60	    repo_url: "/repos/chiron",
61	    base_ref: "main",
62	    brief_id: "CHIRON-RUFF-001",
63	    brief: "Add the missing ruff diagnostics adapter.",
64	    design_notes: "biome.rs is the compiled reference; adapter/declarative is the TOML style.",
65	    acceptance: [
66	      "ruff JSON output parses into DiagnosticEvents",
67	      "the adapter is registered for *.py patterns",
68	    ],
69	    dev_review_cap: 5,
70	    gate_cap: 3,
71	  )
72	}
73	
74	/// The all-green baseline: provisioning succeeds deterministically, the
75	/// scout plans, the dev echoes its prompt into the report, the review
76	/// passes, the gate passes, the land commits.
77	pub fn passing() -> Handlers {
78	  Handlers(
79	    provision: fn(input) {
80	      Ok(io.Workspace(
81	        path: "/work/" <> input.brief_id,
82	        branch: "agent-dev/" <> input.brief_id,
83	      ))
84	    },
85	    scout: fn(_prompt) {
86	      Ok("PLAN: add the ruff adapter beside the biome adapter")
87	    },
88	    dev: fn(prompt) { Ok("DEV-REPORT\n" <> prompt) },
89	    review: fn(_prompt) { Ok(pass_verdict_text) },
90	    gate: fn(_workspace) { Ok(io.GateDetail(pass: True, diagnostics: "")) },
91	    land: fn(_input) { Ok(io.LandOutput(commit_sha: "cafe1234")) },
92	  )
93	}
94	
95	/// A handler for an activity the scenario asserts NEVER runs: reaching it
96	/// fails the dispatch loudly, which fails the test through the workflow's
97	/// typed stage error.
98	pub fn must_not_run(
99	  name: String,
100	) -> fn(input) -> Result(output, error.ActivityError) {
101	  fn(_input) {
102	    Error(error.terminal(
103	      "the `" <> name <> "` activity must not run in this scenario",
104	    ))
105	  }
106	}
107	
108	/// Fresh harness env with every activity's scenario handler registered.
109	pub fn register(handlers: Handlers) -> Nil {
110	  let assert Ok(env) = testing.new()
111	  let workspace = io.Workspace(path: "", branch: "")
112	  let assert Ok(_) =
113	    testing.mock_activity(
114	      env,
115	      activities.provision(io.ProvisionInput(
116	        repo_url: "",
117	        base_ref: "",
118	        brief_id: "",
119	        run_id: "",
120	      )),
121	      handlers.provision,
122	    )
123	  let assert Ok(_) =
124	    testing.mock_activity(env, activities.scout(""), as_outcome(handlers.scout))
125	  let assert Ok(_) =
126	    testing.mock_activity(env, activities.dev(""), as_outcome(handlers.dev))
127	  let assert Ok(_) =
128	    testing.mock_activity(
129	      env,
130	      activities.review(""),
131	      as_outcome(handlers.review),
132	    )
133	  let assert Ok(_) =
134	    testing.mock_activity(env, activities.gate(workspace), handlers.gate)
135	  let assert Ok(_) =
136	    testing.mock_activity(
137	      env,
138	      activities.land(io.LandInput(workspace: workspace, brief_id: "")),
139	      handlers.land,
140	    )
141	  Nil
142	}
143	
144	/// Wraps a scenario's TEXT handler in the same mapping the production
145	/// worker's harness boundary performs: the agent's terminal text becomes the
146	/// canonical agent-outcome record's `text`, with `end_turn` as the completed
147	/// round's canonical stop reason and a fake session handle standing in for
148	/// the one the real harness mints. Errors pass through untouched.
149	fn as_outcome(
150	  handler: fn(String) -> Result(String, error.ActivityError),
151	) -> fn(String) -> Result(AgentOutcome, error.ActivityError) {
152	  fn(prompt) {
153	    case handler(prompt) {
154	      Ok(text) ->
155	        Ok(AgentOutcome(
156	          text: text,
157	          stop_reason: "end_turn",
158	          session_id: "sess-test-agent-dev",
159	        ))
160	      Error(failure) -> Error(failure)
161	    }
162	  }
163	}

5	//// the deployed workflow uses, with the test's handlers standing where the
6	//// agent-dev worker stands in production. `passing/0` is the baseline;
7	//// scenarios override individual handlers with a record update.
8	////
9	//// Operator turns are pre-queued with `signal.send` BEFORE the workflow
10	//// body runs: the test FFI double queues per-name signal payloads FIFO and
11	//// each `signal.receive` consumes the next one, so a scenario scripts the
12	//// whole operator side up front (queue AFTER `register`, which resets the
13	//// process-scoped environment). `queue_raw_continuation` enqueues an
14	//// arbitrary raw payload on the control signal, the seam for exercising the
15	//// workflow's tolerance of undecodable operator payloads.
16	////
17	//// The default assistant handler ECHOES its prompt into the reply, so a
18	//// scenario can observe (statelessly) exactly which prompt each round
19	//// carried. `counter_next` (test FFI, process-dictionary scoped) is the
20	//// seam for counting dispatches.

22	import aion/agent.{type AgentOutcome, AgentOutcome}
23	import aion/codec
24	import aion/error
25	import aion/signal
26	import aion/testing
27	import assistant
28	import assistant/activities
29	import assistant_codecs as codecs
30	import assistant_io as io
31	import gleam/option.{None, Some}
32	
33	/// One handler per activity the session dispatches. The assistant handler
34	/// returns the canonical agent-outcome record, exactly as the worker's
35	/// harness boundary does since #181.
36	pub type Handlers {
37	  Handlers(
38	    provision: fn(io.ProvisionInput) ->
39	      Result(io.Workspace, error.ActivityError),
40	    assistant: fn(String) -> Result(AgentOutcome, error.ActivityError),
41	  )
42	}
43	
44	/// Per-process invocation counter (1 on the first call for a key). The
45	/// harness runs handlers in the test's own process, so this is test-scoped.
46	@external(erlang, "assistant_test_ffi", "counter_next")
47	pub fn counter_next(key: String) -> Int

51	  io.Input(
52	    objective: "How do I add a signal to my order workflow?",
53	    repo_path: "/repos/aion",
54	  )
55	}
56	
57	/// The baseline: provisioning succeeds deterministically (the test double's
58	/// workflow id keys the directory, mirroring production) and the assistant
59	/// echoes its prompt into the reply text of a completed (`end_turn`) outcome.
60	pub fn passing() -> Handlers {
61	  Handlers(
62	    provision: fn(input) { Ok(io.Workspace(path: "/work/" <> input.run_id)) },
63	    assistant: fn(prompt) {
64	      Ok(AgentOutcome(
65	        text: "REPLY\n" <> prompt,
66	        stop_reason: "end_turn",
67	        session_id: "sess-test-assistant",
68	      ))
69	    },
70	  )
71	}
72	
73	/// Fresh harness env with both activities' scenario handlers registered.
74	pub fn register(handlers: Handlers) -> Nil {
75	  let assert Ok(env) = testing.new()
76	  let assert Ok(_) =
77	    testing.mock_activity(
78	      env,
79	      activities.provision(io.ProvisionInput(repo_path: "", run_id: "")),
80	      handlers.provision,
81	    )
82	  let assert Ok(_) =
83	    testing.mock_activity(env, activities.assistant(""), handlers.assistant)
84	  Nil
85	}
86	
87	/// Queue an operator continuation turn on the control signal.
88	pub fn queue_message(message: String) -> Nil {
89	  queue_continuation(io.Continuation(message: Some(message), end: None))
90	}
91	
92	/// Queue the operator's clean end on the control signal.
93	pub fn queue_end() -> Nil {
94	  queue_continuation(io.Continuation(message: None, end: Some(True)))
95	}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	#
3	# The house battery: every gate this repository has, in one command.
4	#
5	# WHY THIS EXISTS
6	#
7	# GitHub Actions is disabled on this repository, so no workflow in
8	# `.github/workflows/` has ever run. That turned out to matter three separate
9	# times, each the same shape — a correctly designed gate that executed nowhere:
10	#
11	#   * the all-features Rust gate, which existed and had never run;
12	#   * `wire-types-no-diff`, whose comment shows its author saw the exact trap it
13	#     was guarding and designed around it — in a lane that is off;
14	#   * the Python and TypeScript SDK proto-drift gates, which are the REMEDIATION
15	#     for an incident where both worker SDKs went wire-dead with green suites.
16	#
17	# Before this script there was no justfile, no Makefile, and no runnable
18	# equivalent, so "the battery" was whatever each person remembered to type. The
19	# Rust battery is what people type, and `cargo test --workspace` does not run
20	# pytest, does not run bun, and does not typecheck the console. Every gate
21	# outside Rust was therefore load-bearing and unexecuted.
22	#
23	# HOW IT REPORTS
24	#
25	# Every gate runs even if an earlier one fails — a battery that stops at the
26	# first failure hides the other three. Each gate's exit code is printed in a
27	# manifest at the end, and the script exits non-zero if ANY gate failed.
28	#
29	# A MISSING TOOLCHAIN IS A FAILURE, NOT A SKIP. A skip is how a gate becomes
30	# invisible, which is the exact defect this script exists to fix. If `uv` or
31	# `bun` is absent the battery says so and goes red; install them or run the
32	# gates you can and say which ones in your report.
33	
34	set -uo pipefail
35	
36	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
37	cd "$REPO_ROOT" || exit 1
38	
39	# Gate name → exit code, in declaration order. Bash 3.2 (macOS system bash) has
40	# no associative arrays, so this is two parallel arrays rather than one map.
41	GATE_NAMES=()
42	GATE_CODES=()
43	
44	# Runs one gate, records its exit code, and never lets a failure stop the run.
45	#
46	# `set +e` around the invocation is deliberate: `set -e` is NOT set for this
47	# script precisely so a red gate cannot abort the battery, and this makes that
48	# explicit at the call site rather than relying on it.
49	gate() {
50	  local name="$1"
51	  shift
52	  printf '\n=== %s ===\n' "$name"
53	  "$@"
54	  local code=$?
55	  GATE_NAMES+=("$name")
56	  GATE_CODES+=("$code")
57	  # `printf` is given the leading dashes as an ARGUMENT, not inside the format
58	  # string: bash's printf reads a format beginning with `--` as an option
59	  # terminator and refuses the call.
60	  printf '%s %s exit %d %s\n' '---' "$name" "$code" '---'
61	  return 0
62	}
63	
64	# Runs a gate inside a directory without leaking the `cd` into later gates.
65	#
66	# The `cd` happens in a subshell rather than via `env -C`, which BSD `env` did
67	# not carry until recently and which would fail on an older macOS with a
68	# message that looks nothing like the real problem.
69	gate_in() {
70	  local name="$1"
71	  local dir="$2"
72	  shift 2
73	  if [ ! -d "$dir" ]; then
74	    printf '\n=== %s ===\n' "$name"
75	    printf 'MISSING DIRECTORY: %s\n' "$dir"
76	    GATE_NAMES+=("$name")
77	    GATE_CODES+=(127)
78	    return 0
79	  fi
80	  gate "$name" bash -c 'cd "$1" && shift && "$@"' _ "$dir" "$@"
81	}
82	
83	# Fails the battery loudly when a required tool is absent, rather than skipping.
84	require_tool() {
85	  local tool="$1"
86	  local why="$2"
87	  if command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
88	    return 0
89	  fi
90	  printf '\n=== toolchain: %s ===\n' "$tool"
91	  printf 'NOT INSTALLED. %s\n' "$why"
92	  printf 'This is a FAILURE, not a skip: a gate that cannot run is a gate that
93	proves nothing, and silently skipping it is how three gates in this repository
94	ended up correct and unexecuted.\n'
95	  GATE_NAMES+=("toolchain:$tool")
96	  GATE_CODES+=(127)
97	  return 1
98	}
99	
100	printf 'aion house battery — repo root %s\n' "$REPO_ROOT"
101	printf 'HEAD %s\n' "$(git rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
102	
103	# The battery's own failure path, executable.
104	#
105	# A reporting harness whose red path has never run is the same defect as a gate
106	# whose assert half has never run — and this repository has now produced three
107	# of those. `AION_BATTERY_SELF_TEST=1 scripts/battery.sh` runs one passing and
108	# one failing synthetic gate and MUST exit 1 with `1 of 2 gates failed`. If it
109	# ever exits 0, this script cannot report a real failure either.
110	if [ "${AION_BATTERY_SELF_TEST:-}" = "1" ]; then
111	  printf 'SELF-TEST MODE: no real gate runs. Expect exit 1 and 1 of 2 failed.\n'
112	  gate "self-test:passes" true
113	  gate "self-test:fails" false
114	else
115	
116	# --- Rust ---------------------------------------------------------------------
117	
118	gate "rust:fmt" cargo fmt --all -- --check
119	gate "rust:clippy" cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
120	
121	# `--no-fail-fast` IS LOAD-BEARING, and its absence cost a P0 on 2026-07-31.
122	#
123	# This script already refuses to stop at the first failing GATE, for the reason
124	# in the header: a battery that stops early hides the gates behind it. Without
125	# this flag the Rust gates broke that same rule one level down — `cargo test`
126	# stops at the first failing TARGET, so a single red lib test silently un-runs
127	# every integration target after it.
128	#
129	# That is not hypothetical. A red lib test in `aion-server` truncated a run
130	# before any integration target started, and the reading — "688 passed, 1
131	# failed" — was taken as one known exception on an otherwise green suite. It was
132	# a truncated run reported as a complete one, and among the targets that never
133	# executed was one that would have HUNG FOREVER on a P0 introduced the day
134	# before (every liminal worker accepting dispatches and executing none). See
135	# docs/design/aion-authoring/RED-MAIN-118-RECORD.md.
136	#
137	# A count is only a coverage claim if the run reached the end. Read the target
138	# list, not the tally.
139	# Runs a cargo test invocation and asserts the run REACHED THE END (#120).
140	#
141	# A test run's exit code and its tally are two different claims, and only the
142	# first is about completeness. `--no-fail-fast` continues past failing tests, but
143	# a target that dies — or a run cut short — simply stops producing output, and
144	# the surviving tally still reads `0 failed`. That is how "688 passed, 1 failed"
145	# was taken as one known exception on an otherwise green suite when it was in
146	# fact a truncated run reported as a complete one, hiding a P0 (see the comment
147	# above `rust:test`).
148	#
149	# 🔴 THE OBVIOUS CONTROL — comparing the COUNT of target-start lines against the
150	# count of `test result:` lines — DOES NOT WORK, and this was measured rather
151	# than assumed. On fully green runs the two disagree:
152	#
153	#     .evidence/118/battery-final.log        45 targets, 48 results
154	#     .evidence/118/shakedown-allfeatures    240 targets, 243 results
155	#
156	# Because a test that RE-EXECUTES ITS OWN BINARY as a child prints the child's
157	# `running N tests` / `test result:` into the parent's stdout, mid-target — e.g.
158	# `config::load::home_tests::aion_home_env_probe_child` from the AION_HOME work.
159	# A counting gate would fire on every green run; worse, a real truncation
160	# coinciding with N child extras would net to zero and read as complete.
161	#
162	# So assert the PAIRING, not the count: every target-start line must be followed
163	# by at least one `test result:` before the next target line. Child extras land
164	# inside a target's own block and are tolerated by construction; a truncation
165	# leaves a started target with nothing after it.
166	#
167	# Validated both ways before being wired in: `unpaired=0` on three real green
168	# logs (including both counting-mismatch cases above) and `unpaired=1` on the
169	# same log with one result line removed.
170	#
171	# Note the filter trap: a legitimately filtered top-level run also reports
172	# `filtered out > 0`, so that field cannot be used to identify child lines — the
173	# `posture:*` gates filter deliberately.
174	#
175	# 🔴 TWO NOUNS THAT LOOK LIKE ONE, both consequences of those same child
176	# re-invocations. Worked out at two hands on the 2026-08-01 green run and
177	# written here because the next person re-derives them from scratch otherwise:
178	#
179	#   * `N passed` is a count of PASS EVENTS, not of DISTINCT TESTS. A subprocess
180	#     test passes twice — once inside its parent target's tally, once as the
181	#     filtered child. That run reported 3952 passed; distinct is ~3949.
182	#   * VERDICT LINES ARE NOT TARGETS. The same run had 243 `test result:` lines
183	#     and 240 targets; the gap is exactly the 3 nested child verdicts.
184	#
185	# Which is why this control counts TARGETS and pairs them rather than summing a
186	# column: a nested child verdict cannot reach it. Summing across verdict lines
187	# treats child re-invocations as peers of top-level runs, and an aggregate over
188	# heterogeneous rows is a number about no population at all. (The same run's
189	# `2133 filtered out` is 3 x 711 from one self-filtering binary — it looks like a
190	# third of the suite was skipped and nothing was.)
191	#
192	# And the pattern needs its COLON. `grep '^test result'` also matches a test
193	# NAMED `result_...`, which is how the 244-vs-243 discrepancy arose in the first
194	# place. Count `^test result:`.
195	paired_test() {
196	  local log
197	  log=$(mktemp) || return 1
198	  "$@" 2>&1 | tee "$log"
199	  local code=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
200	
201	  local counts targets unpaired
202	  counts=$(awk '
203	    /^[[:space:]]+Running |^[[:space:]]+Doc-tests / { if (started) unpaired++; started = 1; targets++ }
204	    /^test result:/ { started = 0 }
205	    END { if (started) unpaired++; print targets + 0, unpaired + 0 }
206	  ' "$log")
207	  targets=${counts%% *}
208	  unpaired=${counts##* }
209	  rm -f "$log"

401	# therefore its content hash.

404	# structural rather than a one-off:

407	#   (no matches)

411	# REPOSITORY AT ALL — a dependency bump anywhere in the tree flips it and our
412	# change is a lockfile line. It has already cost two red goldens once, when the
413	# same `.awl` source compiled to a different package version depending on an
414	# unrelated crate sharing the build.
415	#
416	# 🔴 WHY THE EXISTING COVERAGE IS AN ACCIDENT, NOT A GATE. The ON case does run
417	# today — `rust:test-all-features` above resolves it ON, and `-p <crate>` leaves
418	# it OFF. That disagreement is the ONLY reason the incident was caught. But
419	# nothing states that both resolutions are required, so the detection evaporates
420	# the day the acp crate stops being a workspace member, or the day someone reads
421	# a per-crate green and stops. These gates give it a name.
422	#
423	# 🔴 AND UNDER `OFF`, EVERY `*_independent_of_insertion_order` TEST IS VACUOUS.
424	# `Map` is a `BTreeMap`, so a fixture built `alpha, beta, gamma` and one built
425	# `gamma, beta, alpha` are not two objects — they are the same object, and
426	# asserting they serialize alike compares a value with itself. Those tests read
427	# identically whether they prove something or nothing, which is why the ON run
428	# has to be pinned by name rather than left to resolution.

430	# The posture is detected by BEHAVIOUR, not by a `cfg`. A crate can only `cfg` on
431	# its own features, so a forwarding `preserve-order` feature would report `false`
432	# while the feature was ON in the unification case — a label that lies in exactly
433	# the situation it exists to detect. See crates/aion-package/src/build_coverage.rs.

#
# Five tests used `#[ignore]`, which the house rules ban outright. Among them
# were the CROSS-NODE kill-9 failover proof and the PARKED-TIMER resume proof —
# the two tests that establish the durability claim — so the headline number
# excluded them and nobody reading it could tell.
#
# They are now runtime-gated (`AION_RUN_COSTLY_TESTS=1` to opt in) and each
# announces, on the real stderr handle, WHICH PROOF did not happen. Default
# behaviour is deliberately unchanged: they still do not run. What changed is
# that the run says so.
#
# 🔴 THE HONEST COST, AND WHY THIS GATE IS NOT OPTIONAL. A runtime-gated skip
# returns `Ok(())`, so it counts as a PASS — the total now includes tests that
# proved nothing, which is worse than `#[ignore]`'s separate tally. That trade is
# only acceptable while the announcement is CHECKED. Delete this gate and the
# conversion becomes a downgrade.
#
# 🔴 THE PATTERN MUST MATCH AN ANNOUNCEMENT, NOT THE TOKEN. Found by the
# inverted control, which is the only reason it is not still here: grepping the
# bare token `COSTLY_PROOF_SKIPPED` also matches CARGO'S OWN DIAGNOSTICS, because
# a dead-code warning quotes the source line that defines the constant —
# `pub const SKIP_TOKEN: &str = "COSTLY_PROOF_SKIPPED";`. And that warning
# appears exactly when a call site is removed, so the count was inflated in
# precisely the case the gate exists to detect. The anchored
# `^COSTLY_PROOF_SKIPPED (PROVES NOTHING):` cannot match a quoted source line,
# which compilers indent.
#
# 🔴 A BASELINE IS ONLY A CONTROL IF IT IS INDEPENDENT OF WHAT IT MEASURES.
# The second defect the inverted control found, and the one that would have
# shipped a FALSE PASS. With the pattern fixed, this gate derived its expected
# count by grepping the number of `skip_unless_opted_in(` call sites and
# comparing it to the number of announcements — on the reasoning that a derived
# baseline beats a hardcoded list. It reported `4 call sites, 4 announcements`
# and PASSED while a durability proof was being skipped silently, because
# deleting the call site DELETED ITS OWN EXPECTATION. Two numbers moving
# together, agreeing perfectly about nothing.
#
# So the list below is deliberate. Enumerate the POPULATION — nothing else in
# the tree states which suites own a costly proof — and never the ANSWER. Adding
# a sixth costly proof does require an edit here; that is the price of an
# expectation the code under test cannot move. The non-vacuity guard still
# matters for the same reason it always does: an empty list would assert nothing
# while reporting success, so zero checked suites is a failure.
costly_announcements() {
  # The declared list of suites that carry a costly proof. This IS the
  # enumeration, and it has to be: nothing else in the tree says which suites
  # own one. What must never be enumerated is the ANSWER — see below.
  local targets="lsub5b_osproc_failover_e2e lsub5b_osproc_kill9_failover_e2e \
                 parked_timer_osproc_kill9_failover_e2e stacked_dev_live_e2e \
                 new_scaffold_build"
  local target out found failures=0 checked=0

  for target in $targets; do
    out=$(cargo test -q -p aion-cli --test "$target" 2>&1)
    found=$(printf '%s' "$out" | grep -c '^COSTLY_PROOF_SKIPPED (PROVES NOTHING):')
    checked=$((checked + 1))
    if [ "$found" -eq 0 ]; then
      printf 'COSTLY-ANNOUNCEMENT GATE FAILED: `%s` announced NOTHING.\n' "$target"
      printf 'Its costly proof is being skipped silently — the exact invisibility\n'
      printf '`#[ignore]` was banned for. Either it now runs (move it off this list)\n'
      printf 'or its runtime gate lost its announcement.\n'
      failures=$((failures + 1))
    else
      printf '  %-42s announced %d\n' "$target" "$found"
    fi
  done

  if [ "$checked" -eq 0 ]; then
    printf 'NON-VACUITY GUARD FAILED: the target list is empty, so this gate\n'
    printf 'asserted nothing while reporting success.\n'
    return 1
  fi
  if [ "$failures" -ne 0 ]; then
    printf '%d of %d costly suite(s) failed to announce.\n' "$failures" "$checked"
    return 1
  fi
  printf 'costly announcements ok: %d suite(s), every one announced its skipped proof\n' "$checked"
  # 🔴 SAY THE DIRECTION OUT LOUD. A gated skip PASSES, so converting these off
  # `#[ignore]` RAISED the workspace pass total (3952 -> 3956: +5 now-running
  # announcers, -1 unrelated network failure) while coverage did not move at
  # all. A reader diffing the two totals concludes coverage improved. It did
  # not — honesty improved, and the true proven count is LOWER than either
  # total implies, because these five passes are known non-proofs.
  #
  # A METRIC THAT MOVES OPPOSITE TO THE TRUTH IT ENCODES IS WORSE THAN ONE THAT
  # DOES NOT MOVE. The gate cannot fix the harness's arithmetic, so it states
  # the correction next to the number, every run, where the reader is.
  printf '⚠️  those %d suite(s) PASSED WITHOUT PROVING ANYTHING. Subtract %d from any\n' \
    "$checked" "$checked"
  printf '    pass total before reading it as coverage — making a gap VISIBLE raises\n'
  printf '    the count, so a rising total here is not a coverage win.\n'
  return 0
}

log="gate-logs/241-remediation/gleam-gate-red.log"
exec > >(tee "$log") 2>&1
printf "# #241 Gleam battery-gate red proof\n"
printf "timestamp_utc=%s\n" "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
printf "head=%s\n" "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"

printf "platform=%s\n" "$(uname -a)"
printf "box_load=%s\n" "$(uptime)"
printf "logical_cpus=%s\n" "$(sysctl -n hw.logicalcpu 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
printf "memory_bytes=%s\n" "$(sysctl -n hw.memsize 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
printf "gleam=%s\n" "$(gleam --version 2>&1)"
names="gleam:aion-flow gleam:assistant gleam:agent-dev"
dirs="gleam/aion_flow examples/assistant examples/agent-dev"
codes=""
overall=0
index=1
for dir in $dirs; do
  name=$(printf "%s\n" $names | sed -n "${index}p")
  printf "\n=== %s ===\n" "$name"
  (cd "$dir" && gleam test)
  code=$?
  codes="$codes $code"
  printf "%s %s exit %d %s\n" "---" "$name" "$code" "---"
  [ "$code" -eq 0 ] || overall=1
  index=$((index + 1))
done
printf "\n================ GLEAM GATE MANIFEST ================\n"
set -- $codes
index=1
for name in $names; do
  eval code=\${$index}
  if [ "$code" -eq 0 ]; then verdict=PASS; else verdict=FAIL; fi
  printf "  %-4s  %-20s exit %s\n" "$verdict" "$name" "$code"
  index=$((index + 1))
done
printf "=====================================================\n"
exit "$overall"

1	//! Generic mixed worker for the `agent_dev` proof.
2	//!
3	//! Serves two kinds of activity over the liminal server-push transport
4	//! ([`aion_worker::serve_with_redial`], same wiring as `norn-fan-worker`):
5	//!
6	//! - AGENT activities `scout`, `dev`, `review` (the `agent_dev` workflow)
7	//!   and `assistant` (the `assistant` workflow): routed through the composed
8	//!   [`NornHarness`] (observable + intervenable). Input is the prompt string,
9	//!   output the canonical agent-outcome record
10	//!   (`aion_core::AgentOutcome`: `text` + `stop_reason` + `session_id`). Each run's Norn session id is
11	//!   `{workflow_id}-{activity_type}` and its `--workspace-root` AND `-C`
12	//!   (tool-execution cwd) are the run's own clone
13	//!   `<workspace root>/{workflow_id}/repo` — the placeholders are expanded per
14	//!   run by the adapter, and the workspace root is the SAME resolved root the
15	//!   provision handlers clone under (resolved once here, threaded to both).
16	//!   The session id carries the activity TYPE, not the attempt: every
17	//!   dispatch of the same type in one run resumes ONE session, which is what
18	//!   makes the assistant's multi-round conversation continuous.
19	//! - PLAIN registry activities `provision`, `gate`, `land`: async handler
20	//!   bodies in [`agent_dev_worker::handlers`] whose command process groups are
21	//!   stopped and verified on activity cancellation. The `assistant` workflow's
22	//!   `assistant_provision` is NOT served here: it carries a declared body, so
23	//!   the server executes it from the deployed contract.
24	//!
25	//! Auth: Norn is invoked with `OPENAI_API_KEY` REMOVED from its child
26	//! environment (via the adapter's `without_env`) so it uses the operator's
27	//! `ChatGPT` OAuth login — a stray ambient key would take precedence and fail.
28	//!
29	//! Usage:
30	//!   agent-dev-worker --address 127.0.0.1:PORT [--address 127.0.0.1:PORT2 ...]
31	//!                    [--identity <id>] [--ready-file <path>] [--norn-bin <path>]

1	//// Typed activity constructors for the agent-dev pipeline.
2	////
3	//// Every activity here is served by the agent-dev worker in production. The
4	//// scout/dev/review agent activities speak the canonical agent-outcome
5	//// contract: ONE prompt string in, the `aion/agent.AgentOutcome` record out
6	//// (`text` + `stop_reason` + `session_id`) — the workflow composes every prompt, threads
7	//// each outcome's TEXT, and decodes the review verdict defensively
8	//// (`agent_dev/verdict`). The worker pins one norn session per role per run,
9	//// so a resume round's lean feedback-only prompt lands in the same session
10	//// that did the original work.
11	////
12	//// The local implementations carried by each `activity.new` are terminal
13	//// errors on purpose: this package ships no second, in-process
14	//// implementation of the worker. The `aion/testing` suites register their
15	//// own scenario handlers with `testing.mock_activity`; a dispatch that
16	//// reaches one of these stubs is a test that forgot to register a handler,
17	//// and it fails loudly saying so.
18	
19	import agent_dev_codecs as codecs
20	import agent_dev_io as io
21	import aion/activity
22	import aion/agent.{type AgentOutcome}
23	import aion/codec
24	import aion/duration
25	import aion/error
26	import gleam/dynamic/decode
27	import gleam/json
28	
29	/// The retry policy every step in this pipeline carries for RETRYABLE
30	/// failures (worker death/restart mid-step, a lost connection): a few fixed
31	/// re-deliveries. Safe for the agent steps because the worker pins one norn
32	/// session per role per run (`--resume-if-exists`): a retried step resumes
33	/// the SAME session and its accumulated work, never starting over. Terminal
34	/// failures (a real harness error) are not retried.
35	fn survives_worker_restart(
36	  step: activity.Activity(i, o),
37	) -> activity.Activity(i, o) {
38	  activity.retry(
39	    step,
40	    activity.RetryPolicy(
41	      max_attempts: 3,
42	      backoff: activity.Fixed(delay: duration.seconds(5)),
43	    ),
44	  )
45	}

1	# agent-dev
2	
3	A durable agent dev pipeline whose agent steps run through the norn harness —
4	observable and intervenable. This is the Phase-2 NOI dogfood workflow: one
5	flat workflow, six recorded activities, two bounded loops, honest terminal
6	dispositions.
7	
8	## Flow
9	
10	```
11	provision -> scout -> dev -> review
12	                       ^        |
13	                       +--------+   bounded by dev_review_cap (cumulative)
14	                     gate
15	                       |  fail -> dev(diagnostics) -> [bounded review loop] -> gate
16	                       |            bounded by gate_cap
17	                     land           (Passed ONLY)
18	```
19	
20	- **provision** checks out `repo_url` at `base_ref` into a fresh branch for
21	  the brief and returns the workspace `{path, branch}`.
22	- **scout / dev / review** are agent activities under the canonical
23	  agent-outcome contract: ONE prompt string in, the agent-outcome record out
24	  (`{text, stop_reason, session_id}`; the workflow threads each outcome's text). The
25	  workflow composes every prompt (`src/agent_dev/prompts.gleam`): round one carries
26	  the full contract (brief + design notes + acceptance + scout plan), resume
27	  rounds are lean feedback-only prompts, because the worker pins one norn
28	  session per role per run.
29	- The **review verdict** is decoded defensively (`src/agent_dev/verdict.gleam`):
30	  the reviewer is instructed in-prompt to end with exactly
31	  `{"pass": bool, "blockers": [...], "summary": "..."}`; the workflow parses
32	  a trailing JSON object out of the terminal text, re-asks ONCE ("respond
33	  with only the JSON verdict") on an unparseable reply, and counts a still
34	  unparseable reply as a failed review round.
35	- **gate** runs the authoritative checks; a failing gate is recorded data,
36	  and each failure (budget permitting) drives a dev feedback round, a
37	  re-entry into the bounded review loop, and a re-gate.
38	- **land** merges the branch — dispatched ONLY on a `Passed` disposition.
39	
40	Exhausting a cap is a **disposition** (`review_cap_exhausted` /
41	`gate_cap_exhausted`), never an error: the run completes, `land` is skipped,
42	and the workspace persists for inspection (its `branch` and `workspace_path`
43	ride the output). An `agent_dev_status` query answers live `{phase, round}`
44	at every stage.

281	the proof. The proof is a live agent round on the swapped binary whose agent
282	receives the prompt TEXT — read from the recorded dispatch input and from the
283	agent's own transcript, not from a passing suite. That acceptance is owed, is
284	recorded here as owed, and rides the #228 release swap.

286	---
287	
288	## Amendment — 2026-08-14, task #205: the record gains a third field
289	
290	This document's statements of the canonical agent-outcome record as **two**
291	fields (`AgentOutcome { text: String, stop_reason: String }`, and the
292	"two-field agent action" objection answered above) describe the record as it
293	stood when this ruling was made. They are left as written — this document is
294	the record of a decision, not a living reference.
295	
296	Task #205 (the ACP `session/load` lane, Waffles' approval) widened the record
297	to **three mandatory fields**: `text: String`, `stop_reason: String`, and
298	`session_id: String`. The third field is the handle of the conversation that
299	produced the outcome — a FACT the harness fills from its own session, never a
300	promise the session can be resumed (resumability is the harness's own
301	handshake question), and meaningful only to the harness that minted it;
302	resume routing pairs the id with the harness identity. The widening REPLACED
303	the two-field shape (house rule: no backwards compatibility) — a two-field
304	payload no longer decodes, the checker demands the three-field record
305	structurally, and an empty-string `session_id` is refused by name at
306	`AgentOutcome::into_payload`. Everything else this ruling establishes — the
307	seam belongs in the language, the marker classifies the declaration, the
308	prompt is the parameter's TEXT — stands unchanged.
309	
310	---
311	
312	## Amendment — 2026-08-14, task #241: the final message is distinct
313	
314	Task #241 replaced the three-field record with exactly four mandatory fields: `text: String` is the
315	whole accumulated run output, `final_message: String` is the LAST completed agent answer alone,
316	`stop_reason: String` is the canonical reason, and `session_id: String` is the conversation handle.
317	The distinction prevents exact-token judges from falsely failing a successful run when earlier
318	narration precedes its final verdict. Reasoning, tools, and user turns never enter `final_message`.
319	When there was no answer, `text` and `final_message` are both honestly empty; with one answer they
320	are honestly equal. This is replacement semantics again: a three-field payload no longer decodes

1	//! The canonical agent-outcome record — the ONE shape every agent harness
2	//! emits as a completed agent activity's result.
3	//!
4	//! Task #181's ruling (docs commit `c223c8c`): the `agent` marker had
5	//! universalized one harness path's shape (`-> String`, "parse it
6	//! downstream"), while the harnesses honestly emitted three different ad-hoc
7	//! JSON shapes. The fix is this record, defined by aion, snake_case and
8	//! AWL-expressible: every harness maps its native terminal outcome onto it at
9	//! the integration boundary, and a workflow's `agent` action declares a record
10	//! of exactly this shape and reads `text` / `final_message` / `stop_reason` /
11	//! `session_id` as fields.
12	//!
13	//! Task #205's ruling widened the record with a third mandatory field,
14	//! `session_id` — see [`AgentOutcome::session_id`] for its semantics. The
15	//! widening is a replacement, not an addition: the wire shape is exactly the
16	//! three keys, a two-field payload no longer decodes, and a two-field AWL declaration no longer
17	//! checks. Task #241 replaces that record in turn with a fourth mandatory field,
18	//! `final_message`: [`AgentOutcome::text`] remains the whole accumulated output, while
19	//! [`AgentOutcome::final_message`] is the last completed answer alone. That distinction prevents an
20	//! exact-token judge from falsely failing a successful run merely because earlier narrated answers
21	//! precede the final verdict. The wire shape is now exactly four keys; a three-field payload no
22	//! longer decodes and a three-field AWL declaration no longer checks.
23	//!
24	//! # One stop-reason vocabulary, by subtraction
25	//!
26	//! The canonical `stop_reason` strings are the snake_case renderings of the
27	//! existing neutral [`StopKind`] semantic set — no third stop-reason table
28	//! exists anywhere. [`StopKind::canonical_stop_reason`] is the single mapping,
29	//! so the transcript channel (which carries `StopKind` itself) and this
30	//! outcome record cannot drift. `StopKind`'s own serialization is untouched:
31	//! the transcript wire is live and is a different channel from the result.
32	//!
33	//! # The record rides inside a [`Payload`]
34	//!
35	//! Nothing about the type-erased result path changes: an activity result is
36	//! still a [`Payload`] of `{content_type, bytes}`. The record is the JSON the
37	//! bytes carry for a completed agent activity.
38	
39	use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
40	
41	use crate::activity_event::StopKind;
42	use crate::payload::{ContentType, Payload};
43	
44	impl StopKind {
45	    /// The canonical `snake_case` `stop_reason` string for this stop kind.
46	    ///
47	    /// This is the ONE mapping from the neutral stop vocabulary onto the
48	    /// [`AgentOutcome::stop_reason`] wire strings. The detail payloads of
49	    /// [`StopKind::Error`] and [`StopKind::Other`] deliberately do not reach
50	    /// the canonical string: the canonical vocabulary is closed, and the
51	    /// detail belongs to the transcript channel that carries the full
52	    /// `StopKind`.
53	    #[must_use]
54	    pub fn canonical_stop_reason(&self) -> &'static str {
55	        match self {
56	            Self::EndTurn => "end_turn",
57	            Self::ToolUse => "tool_use",
58	            Self::LimitReached => "limit_reached",
59	            Self::Cancelled => "cancelled",
60	            Self::Error { .. } => "error",
61	            Self::Other { .. } => "other",
62	        }
63	    }
64	}
65	
66	/// The error serializing an [`AgentOutcome`] as its result [`Payload`].
67	#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
68	pub enum AgentOutcomeError {
69	    /// The record's mandatory `session_id` is the empty string.
70	    ///
71	    /// A vacant mandatory field is a harness bug, refused here by name at the
72	    /// one funnel every harness serializes through — never shipped as a
73	    /// silently empty handle a workflow would try to resume with.
74	    #[error(
75	        "the agent-outcome record's mandatory `session_id` is empty — every harness fills it \
76	         with the handle of the conversation that produced this outcome, and an empty handle \
77	         names no conversation"
78	    )]
79	    EmptySessionId,
80	    /// The record could not be encoded as JSON — unreachable for four plain
81	    /// strings, but never swallowed.
82	    #[error("the agent-outcome record is not encodable: {0}")]
83	    Encode(#[from] serde_json::Error),
84	}
85	
86	/// The canonical agent-outcome record: what a completed agent activity's
87	/// result payload carries, from every harness.
88	///
89	/// Four fields, all `snake_case`, all mandatory, all AWL-expressible — the
90	/// AWL checker demands an `agent` action's declared return type be a record of
91	/// exactly this shape (`text: String`, `final_message: String`, `stop_reason: String`,
92	/// `session_id: String`), so a workflow reads those values as ordinary record fields.
93	///
94	/// Empty `text` and `final_message` values on a completed run are honest, not a bug: an agent that
95	/// finished its turn having emitted only tool calls said nothing, and the harness reports that
96	/// truth rather than inventing words (the work is on the transcript). When the run produced exactly
97	/// one completed answer, `final_message == text`; that duplication is the honest degenerate case.
98	/// `stop_reason` is one of the canonical strings produced by [`StopKind::canonical_stop_reason`]:
99	/// `end_turn | tool_use | limit_reached | cancelled | error | other`.
100	#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, ts_rs::TS, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
101	pub struct AgentOutcome {
102	    /// The whole run output: every completed agent answer, accumulated by the harness.
103	    pub text: String,
104	    /// The run's LAST completed agent answer message, alone and exactly as the agent said it.
105	    ///
106	    /// Reasoning, tool output, and user turns never enter this field. It exists separately from
107	    /// [`Self::text`] so an exact-token judge reads the actual final verdict rather than falsely
108	    /// failing a successful run because narration from earlier answers precedes it. It is empty when
109	    /// the agent produced no answer text at all, and equals `text` when there was exactly one answer.
110	    pub final_message: String,
111	    /// The canonical `snake_case` stop reason
112	    /// ([`StopKind::canonical_stop_reason`]).
113	    pub stop_reason: String,
114	    /// The handle of the conversation that produced this outcome.
115	    ///
116	    /// A FACT, not a promise: the id names the session the harness actually
117	    /// ran — minted, loaded, or derived by that harness — and says nothing
118	    /// about whether it can be resumed. Resumability is the per-agent question
119	    /// a harness's own handshake answers (for ACP, the `initialize` response's
120	    /// `loadSession` capability), never something this field asserts.
121	    ///
122	    /// The id is meaningful only to the harness that minted it; resume routing
123	    /// pairs the id with the harness identity the workflow record already
124	    /// carries. It is never empty — a harness with a vacant handle is refused
125	    /// at [`AgentOutcome::into_payload`], not shipped.
126	    pub session_id: String,
127	}
128	
129	impl AgentOutcome {
130	    /// Builds the record from the whole accumulated answer text, the last completed answer alone,
131	    /// the neutral stop kind, and the conversation handle, spelling `stop_reason` through the one
132	    /// canonical mapping.
133	    #[must_use]
134	    pub fn new(
135	        text: impl Into<String>,
136	        final_message: impl Into<String>,
137	        stop: &StopKind,
138	        session_id: impl Into<String>,
139	    ) -> Self {
140	        Self {
141	            text: text.into(),
142	            final_message: final_message.into(),
143	            stop_reason: stop.canonical_stop_reason().to_owned(),
144	            session_id: session_id.into(),
145	        }
146	    }
147	
148	    /// Serializes the record as the activity's JSON result [`Payload`].
149	    ///
150	    /// # Errors
151	    ///
152	    /// [`AgentOutcomeError::EmptySessionId`] when the mandatory `session_id`
153	    /// is the empty string — the vacancy is refused by name rather than
154	    /// shipped. [`AgentOutcomeError::Encode`] when the record cannot be
155	    /// encoded — unreachable for four plain strings, but never swallowed.
156	    pub fn into_payload(self) -> Result<Payload, AgentOutcomeError> {
157	        if self.session_id.is_empty() {
158	            return Err(AgentOutcomeError::EmptySessionId);
159	        }
160	        let bytes = serde_json::to_vec(&self)?;
161	        Ok(Payload::new(ContentType::Json, bytes))
162	    }
163	}
164	
165	#[cfg(test)]
166	mod tests {
167	    use serde_json::json;
168	
169	    use super::{AgentOutcome, AgentOutcomeError, StopKind};
170	
171	    type TestResult = Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>;
172	
173	    /// The canonical vocabulary is the closed set the ruling names, spelled by
174	    /// exactly one mapping. Enumerated over every variant so a new `StopKind`
175	    /// arm cannot ship without a canonical spelling.
176	    #[test]
177	    fn every_stop_kind_has_its_canonical_snake_case_spelling() {
178	        let cases = [
179	            (StopKind::EndTurn, "end_turn"),
180	            (StopKind::ToolUse, "tool_use"),
181	            (StopKind::LimitReached, "limit_reached"),
182	            (StopKind::Cancelled, "cancelled"),
183	            (
184	                StopKind::Error {
185	                    message: "boom".to_owned(),
186	                },
187	                "error",
188	            ),
189	            (
190	                StopKind::Other {
191	                    reason: "teleported".to_owned(),
192	                },
193	                "other",
194	            ),
195	        ];
196	        for (kind, expected) in cases {
197	            assert_eq!(kind.canonical_stop_reason(), expected);
198	        }
199	    }
200	
201	    /// The wire form is exactly the four `snake_case` keys the AWL record
202	    /// declares — this is the shape every harness emits and every workflow
203	    /// decodes, so it is pinned as JSON, not as a Rust round-trip alone.

15	@internal

17	  Dispatched(correlation_id: String, output_codec: codec.Codec(o))
18	}

20	type SettledDispatch(o) {
21	  SettledDispatch(Dispatched(o))

26	pub fn run(
27	  activity_value: Activity(i, o),
28	  workflow_default_task_queue: option.Option(String),
29	) -> Result(o, error.ActivityError) {
30	  use dispatched <- result.try(dispatch(
31	    activity_value,
32	    workflow_default_task_queue,
33	  ))
34	  await(dispatched)
35	}

37	@internal
38	pub fn all_settled(
39	  activities: List(Activity(i, o)),
40	  workflow_default_task_queue: option.Option(String),
41	) -> List(Result(o, error.ActivityError)) {
42	  let dispatched =
43	    list.map(activities, fn(activity_value) {
44	      case settled_policy_supported(activity_value) {
45	        False -> SettledRefused(settled_policy_error())
46	        True ->
47	          case dispatch(activity_value, workflow_default_task_queue) {
48	            Ok(value) -> SettledDispatch(value)
49	            Error(failure) -> SettledRefused(failure)
50	          }
51	      }
52	    })
53	  list.map(dispatched, fn(value) {
54	    case value {
55	      SettledDispatch(dispatched) -> await(dispatched)
56	      SettledRefused(failure) -> Error(failure)
57	    }
58	  })
59	}

61	/// Encode, configure, and dispatch one activity on its selected tier.
62	fn dispatch(

65	) -> Result(Dispatched(o), error.ActivityError) {

67	  let encoded_input = input_codec.encode(activity.input(activity_value))

69	  let dispatched = case activity.selected_tier(activity_value) {
70	    Some(activity.InVm) ->
71	      ffi.dispatch_activity_in_vm(
72	        activity.name(activity_value),
73	        encoded_input,
74	        config,
75	        in_vm_thunk(activity_value),
76	      )
77	    Some(activity.RemotePython) | Some(activity.RemoteRust) | None ->
78	      ffi.dispatch_activity(
79	        activity.name(activity_value),
80	        encoded_input,
81	        config,
82	      )
83	  }
84	  case dispatched {
85	    Ok(correlation_id) ->
86	      Ok(Dispatched(correlation_id, activity.output_codec(activity_value)))
87	    Error(raw_error) -> Error(parse_error(raw_error))
88	  }
89	}

91	/// Await and decode one previously dispatched activity.
92	fn await(dispatched: Dispatched(o)) -> Result(o, error.ActivityError) {
93	  let Dispatched(correlation_id, output_codec) = dispatched

101	      }

1	//! The shared run read.
2	//!
3	//! Every tool that needs to know something about a run gets it from HERE, from
4	//! ONE namespace-gated history read. Two reads would be two answers that could
5	//! disagree — and one of them would be the one the agent acted on.
6	
7	use aion_core::{Event, RunId, WorkflowId, WorkflowSummary};
8	use aion_mcp::tools::service::{ToolCall, ToolFailure};
9	use aion_proto::{ProtoDescribeWorkflowRequest, ProtoWorkflowId, WireError};
10	use serde_json::json;
11	
12	use crate::mcp::args::{optional_run_id, required_str, required_workflow_id};
13	use crate::mcp::run_scope::RunScope;
14	use crate::{CallerIdentity, ServerState, api::handlers};
15	
16	use super::errors::tool_failure;
17	
18	/// One namespace-gated read of a workflow, projected for the tools.
19	pub(crate) struct RunView {
20	    /// The namespace the caller was scoped to.
21	    pub(crate) namespace: String,
22	    /// The workflow that was read.
23	    pub(crate) workflow_id: WorkflowId,
24	    /// The run this view is about: the caller's, or the latest of the chain
25	    /// when the caller named none.
26	    pub(crate) run_id: RunId,
27	    /// The workflow's complete history, across every run of the chain.
28	    pub(crate) history: Vec<Event>,
29	    /// The status projection over that history.
30	    pub(crate) summary: WorkflowSummary,
31	    /// Which run of the chain dispatched which attempt.
32	    pub(crate) scope: RunScope,
33	}
34	
35	impl RunView {
36	    /// Read a workflow under the caller's authorization.
37	    ///
38	    /// The `run_id` argument is resolved but NOT trusted: a run that is not one
39	    /// of this workflow's own runs is refused here rather than silently read as
40	    /// though it were the latest. Naming another workflow's run and being
41	    /// served this workflow's history is exactly the confusion the required
42	    /// run handle exists to prevent.
43	    ///
44	    /// # Errors
45	    ///
46	    /// [`ToolFailure`] when the arguments are malformed, the caller does not
47	    /// hold the namespace, the workflow does not exist, or the named run is not
48	    /// this workflow's.
49	    pub(crate) async fn read(
50	        state: &ServerState,
51	        caller: &CallerIdentity,
52	        call: &ToolCall,
53	    ) -> Result<Self, ToolFailure> {
54	        let namespace = required_str(call, "namespace")?;
55	        let workflow_id = required_workflow_id(call, "workflow_id")?;
56	        let requested_run = optional_run_id(call, "run_id")?;
57	        Self::read_parts(
58	            state,
59	            caller,
60	            &namespace,
61	            &workflow_id,
62	            requested_run.as_ref(),
63	        )
64	        .await
65	    }
66	
67	    /// The same read from already-extracted parts.
68	    ///
69	    /// # Errors
70	    ///
71	    /// As [`RunView::read`].
72	    pub(crate) async fn read_parts(
73	        state: &ServerState,
74	        caller: &CallerIdentity,
75	        namespace: &str,
76	        workflow_id: &WorkflowId,
77	        requested_run: Option<&RunId>,
78	    ) -> Result<Self, ToolFailure> {
79	        let request = ProtoDescribeWorkflowRequest {
80	            namespace: namespace.to_owned(),
81	            workflow_id: Some(ProtoWorkflowId {
82	                uuid: workflow_id.to_string(),
83	            }),
84	            run_id: requested_run.map(|run| run.clone().into()),
85	            include_history: false,
86	        };
87	        let outcome = handlers::describe(state.namespace_guard(), caller, request)
88	            .await
89	            .map_err(|error| tool_failure(&error))?;
90	        let summary = WorkflowSummary::from_history(&outcome.history).ok_or_else(|| {
91	            tool_failure(&WireError::not_found(format!(
92	                "workflow {workflow_id} has no recorded start event"
93	            )))
94	        })?;
95	        let scope = RunScope::from_history(&outcome.history);
96	        let run_id = match requested_run {
97	            Some(run) => {
98	                if !scope.knows_run(run) {
99	                    return Err(ToolFailure::new(
100	                        format!(
101	                            "run {run} is not a run of workflow {workflow_id}. Call describe_run \
102	                             without a run_id to get this workflow's current run, and never \
103	                             construct a run id."
104	                        ),
105	                        json!({
106	                            "code": "unknown_run",
107	                            "workflow_id": workflow_id.to_string(),
108	                            "run_id": run.to_string(),
109	                        }),
110	                    ));
111	                }
112	                run.clone()
113	            }
114	            None => latest_run(&outcome.history).ok_or_else(|| {
115	                tool_failure(&WireError::not_found(format!(
116	                    "workflow {workflow_id} has no recorded run"
117	                )))
118	            })?,
119	        };
120	        Ok(Self {
121	            namespace: outcome.namespace,
122	            workflow_id: outcome.workflow_id,
123	            run_id,
124	            history: outcome.history,
125	            summary,
126	            scope,
127	        })
128	    }
129	
130	    /// The head sequence of the workflow's history: the seq of its last event.
131	    pub(crate) fn history_head_seq(&self) -> u64 {
132	        self.history.last().map_or(0, Event::seq)
133	    }
134	
135	    /// The events belonging to this view's run alone.
136	    pub(crate) fn run_segment(&self) -> &[Event] {
137	        aion_core::run_segment(&self.history, &self.run_id)
138	    }
139	}
140	
141	/// The last run opened in a history — the newest generation of the chain.
142	fn latest_run(history: &[Event]) -> Option<RunId> {
143	    history.iter().rev().find_map(|event| match event {
144	        Event::WorkflowStarted { run_id, .. } => Some(run_id.clone()),
145	        _ => None,
146	    })
147	}

1	//// The canonical agent-outcome record — the shape every agent harness emits
2	//// as a completed agent activity's result (task #181's ruling).
3	////
4	//// A Gleam-authored workflow that dispatches an agent activity declares its
5	//// output as this record and decodes it with `outcome_codec`: `text` carries the whole
6	//// accumulated output, while `final_message` carries the last completed agent answer alone.
7	//// Both are the honest empty string when the agent finished a round saying nothing, and they are
8	//// equal when the run produced exactly one answer. `stop_reason` carries the canonical snake_case
9	//// stop reason
10	//// (`end_turn | tool_use | limit_reached | cancelled | error | other`),
11	//// spelled by the one Rust-side mapping in `aion-core` — this module defines
12	//// no vocabulary of its own — and `session_id` carries the handle of the
13	//// conversation that produced the outcome. The handle is a fact, not a
14	//// promise: it names the session the harness actually ran and says nothing
15	//// about whether it can be resumed (resumability is the harness's own
16	//// handshake question). It is meaningful only to the harness that minted it;
17	//// resume routing pairs it with the harness identity the workflow record
18	//// already carries.
19	////
20	//// This is the Gleam-side single source of the record, mirrored from
21	//// `aion_core::AgentOutcome`; example packages import it rather than each
22	//// declaring their own copy that could drift.
23	
24	import aion/codec.{type Codec}
25	import gleam/dynamic/decode
26	import gleam/json
27	
28	/// The canonical agent-outcome record: accumulated `text`, the last answer as
29	/// `final_message`, the canonical snake_case `stop_reason`, and the
30	/// `session_id` conversation handle.
31	pub type AgentOutcome {
32	  AgentOutcome(text: String, final_message: String, stop_reason: String, session_id: String)
33	}
34	
35	/// The wire codec for the record: a JSON object of exactly
36	/// `{"text": <string>, "final_message": <string>, "stop_reason": <string>,
37	/// "session_id": <string>}`.
38	pub fn outcome_codec() -> Codec(AgentOutcome) {
39	  codec.json_codec(
40	    fn(outcome: AgentOutcome) {
41	      json.object([
42	        #("text", json.string(outcome.text)),
43	        #("final_message", json.string(outcome.final_message)),
44	        #("stop_reason", json.string(outcome.stop_reason)),
45	        #("session_id", json.string(outcome.session_id)),
46	      ])
47	    },
48	    {
49	      use text <- decode.field("text", decode.string)
50	      use final_message <- decode.field("final_message", decode.string)
51	      use stop_reason <- decode.field("stop_reason", decode.string)
52	      use session_id <- decode.field("session_id", decode.string)
53	      decode.success(AgentOutcome(text:, final_message:, stop_reason:, session_id:))
54	    },
55	  )
56	}

2	"""Generate awl-deck.html from the checked example documents.
3	
4	The deck teaches AWL keyword by keyword. Every snippet on a slide is SLICED
5	out of a complete document under deck-examples/ rather than retyped here, so
6	the deck cannot claim a shape the language does not actually accept: if an
7	example stops checking, this script refuses to write the deck at all.
8	
9	    python3 docs/authoring/build-deck.py
10	
11	Exit status is 0 only when every referenced document passed `aion awl check`
12	and the deck was written.
13	"""
14	
15	from __future__ import annotations
16	
17	import html
18	import shutil
19	import subprocess
20	import sys
21	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
22	from pathlib import Path
23	
24	HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
25	EXAMPLES = HERE / "deck-examples"
26	SHELL = HERE / "deck-shell.html"
27	OUTPUT = HERE / "awl-deck.html"
28	
29	
30	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
31	# Excerpts
32	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
33	
34	
35	@dataclass(frozen=True)
36	class Excerpt:
37	    """A contiguous run of lines from one checked document.
38	
39	    Anchored on substrings rather than line numbers so that editing an example
40	    does not silently shift what a slide shows. A missing anchor is a hard
41	    error, not a truncated slide.
42	    """
43	
44	    document: str
45	    start: str
46	    end: str
47	    dedent: bool = True
48	    # A closing brace or a closing `"""` is a substring of half the file, so an
49	    # anchor may instead demand the whole (stripped) line.

63	/// because these three have no other home yet, and removing their routing here

65	/// than answer it.

68	/// Lower bound on the reconnect backoff between candidate dials.

71	/// adopt the shard and bring its listener up).

74	/// Compose the agent harness at the binary root — the ONE place this worker
75	/// names a concrete [`AgentHarness`](aion_integrations::AgentHarness) adapter,
76	/// mirroring `norn-fan-worker` and the `aion` binary's composition root. The
77	/// serve path drives it only through the erased neutral trait
78	/// ([`DynAgentHarness`]), so swapping the adapter touches this function alone.
79	///
80	/// `workspace_root` is the SAME resolved root the `provision` handler clones
81	/// under: every agent round works inside the run's own clone
82	/// (`<root>/{workflow_id}/repo`). `--workspace-root` confines the file tools
83	/// to that clone, and `-C` sets the tool EXECUTION cwd to the same directory —
84	/// without it the agent's bash commands would run in the worker's own cwd,
85	/// outside the clone. Its session id (`{workflow_id}-{activity_type}` +
86	/// `--resume-if-exists`) is stable per `(run, round)` so a re-dispatch after a
87	/// failover RESUMES the session rather than starting over. `--fast` selects
88	/// Norn's fast model tier.

91	/// adapter's intervention translation supports today (`InjectMessage` +
92	/// `Cancel`); advertising more would promise interventions the harness
93	/// rejects.
94	///
95	/// The argv itself is built by

97	/// asserted directly, and the composed harness is wrapped in

100	fn composed_agent_harness(
101	    norn_bin: &str,
102	    norn_account: &str,
103	    norn_model: Option<&str>,
104	    workspace_root: &Path,
105	    allow_degraded_session: bool,
106	    agent_descriptors: &[aion_package::ActivityDescriptor],
107	    declared_agent_types: &[String],
108	) -> AgentHarnessConfig {
109	    // The run's own clone — the ONE template both the file-tool confinement
110	    // (--workspace-root) and the tool-execution cwd (-C) point at.
111	    let run_clone = format!("{}/{{workflow_id}}/repo", workspace_root.display());
112	    // The PROCESS working directory is the workspace root, not `run_clone`: the
113	    // clone is a per-run template that does not exist until `provision` makes
114	    // it, and a process cannot be started in a directory that is not there yet.
115	    // What the agent READS and EDITS is confined to the clone by
116	    // `--workspace-root`/`-C` above; this only decides where the child stands
117	    // when it is launched, and now it is decided here rather than inherited
118	    // from whichever shell started this worker.
119	    let mut norn = NornHarness::with_binary(norn_bin, workspace_root);
120	    for arg in norn_args(&run_clone, norn_account, norn_model, allow_degraded_session) {
121	        norn = norn.with_arg(arg);
122	    }
123	    let harness: Arc<dyn DynAgentHarness> = Arc::new(AdvisingHarness::new(

125	        // and a stray ambient key would take precedence and fail.
126	        Arc::new(norn.without_env("OPENAI_API_KEY")),

129	        // constant the argument parser accepts.

131	    ));

133	    // undeclared residue named above. Declared names come first because they
134	    // are the ones a reader can check against a source file.
135	    let agent_types: Vec<String> = declared_agent_types

138	        .chain(

140	                .iter()
141	                .map(|&name| name.to_owned()),
142	        )
143	        .collect();

145	        harness,
146	        agent_types,

48	use aion_integration_norn::{AdvisingHarness, NornHarness};
49	use aion_integrations::{DynAgentHarness, InterventionCapabilities, InterventionPrimitive};
50	use aion_worker::{AgentHarnessConfig, RedialTiming, WorkerConfig};
51	use args::parse_args;
52	
53	/// Agent rounds this binary serves for a package that has NO `.awl` document
54	/// to declare them — the three Norn rounds of the Gleam-authored `agent_dev`
55	/// workflow. ONE worker binary serves both packages.
56	///
57	/// Everything the `assistant` document DOES declare now arrives through the
58	/// document's own `agent` markers ([`advertised_surface`]), which is why this
59	/// list no longer contains `assistant`. What remains is the residue of a
60	/// package that cannot state the fact itself.
61	///
62	/// This list is deletable, and the condition is precise: when `agent_dev`
63	/// gains an `.awl` document, mark its three rounds `agent` there and delete
64	/// this constant. It is NOT kept because a Rust list is an acceptable place
65	/// for the fact — the whole point of the marker is that it is not. It is kept
66	/// because these three have no other home yet, and removing their routing here
67	/// would quietly settle an open question about the Gleam authoring path rather
68	/// than answer it.
69	const UNDECLARED_AGENT_ACTIVITY_TYPES: [&str; 3] = ["scout", "dev", "review"];
70	
71	/// Lower bound on the reconnect backoff between candidate dials.
72	const REDIAL_INITIAL_BACKOFF: Duration = Duration::from_millis(50);
73	/// Upper bound on the reconnect backoff (a survivor may take a moment to
74	/// adopt the shard and bring its listener up).
75	const REDIAL_MAX_BACKOFF: Duration = Duration::from_millis(500);
76	
77	/// Compose the agent harness at the binary root — the ONE place this worker
78	/// names a concrete [`AgentHarness`](aion_integrations::AgentHarness) adapter,
79	/// mirroring `norn-fan-worker` and the `aion` binary's composition root. The
80	/// serve path drives it only through the erased neutral trait
81	/// ([`DynAgentHarness`]), so swapping the adapter touches this function alone.
82	///
83	/// `workspace_root` is the SAME resolved root the `provision` handler clones
84	/// under: every agent round works inside the run's own clone
85	/// (`<root>/{workflow_id}/repo`). `--workspace-root` confines the file tools
86	/// to that clone, and `-C` sets the tool EXECUTION cwd to the same directory —
87	/// without it the agent's bash commands would run in the worker's own cwd,
88	/// outside the clone. Its session id (`{workflow_id}-{activity_type}` +
89	/// `--resume-if-exists`) is stable per `(run, round)` so a re-dispatch after a
90	/// failover RESUMES the session rather than starting over. `--fast` selects
91	/// Norn's fast model tier.
92	///
93	/// The advertised capabilities are exactly the neutral primitives the Norn
94	/// adapter's intervention translation supports today (`InjectMessage` +
95	/// `Cancel`); advertising more would promise interventions the harness
96	/// rejects.
97	///
98	/// The argv itself is built by
99	/// [`norn_args`](agent_dev_worker::norn_invocation::norn_args) so it can be
100	/// asserted directly, and the composed harness is wrapped in
101	/// [`AdvisingHarness`] so norn's degraded-session refusal reaches the operator
102	/// with the flag that gets past it.
103	fn composed_agent_harness(
104	    norn_bin: &str,
105	    norn_account: &str,
106	    norn_model: Option<&str>,
107	    workspace_root: &Path,
108	    allow_degraded_session: bool,
109	    agent_descriptors: &[aion_package::ActivityDescriptor],
110	    declared_agent_types: &[String],
111	) -> AgentHarnessConfig {
112	    // The run's own clone — the ONE template both the file-tool confinement
113	    // (--workspace-root) and the tool-execution cwd (-C) point at.
114	    let run_clone = format!("{}/{{workflow_id}}/repo", workspace_root.display());
115	    // The PROCESS working directory is the workspace root, not `run_clone`: the
116	    // clone is a per-run template that does not exist until `provision` makes
117	    // it, and a process cannot be started in a directory that is not there yet.
118	    // What the agent READS and EDITS is confined to the clone by
119	    // `--workspace-root`/`-C` above; this only decides where the child stands
120	    // when it is launched, and now it is decided here rather than inherited
121	    // from whichever shell started this worker.
122	    let mut norn = NornHarness::with_binary(norn_bin, workspace_root);
123	    for arg in norn_args(&run_clone, norn_account, norn_model, allow_degraded_session) {
124	        norn = norn.with_arg(arg);
125	    }
126	    let harness: Arc<dyn DynAgentHarness> = Arc::new(AdvisingHarness::new(
127	        // Force the `ChatGPT` OAuth login: the project does not use API keys,
128	        // and a stray ambient key would take precedence and fail.
129	        Arc::new(norn.without_env("OPENAI_API_KEY")),
130	        allow_degraded_session,
131	        // The advice names THIS worker's restart flag, spelled by the same
132	        // constant the argument parser accepts.
133	        DEGRADED_SESSION_OPT_IN,
134	    ));
